### 10.2. Threats to Validity

#### Construct validity.

Retrieval targets are pre-patch files and callables intersected by developer
patches, so they omit context read without editing, and added-only units are
unretrievable. Q6 measures localization, and Q7’s official tests cannot
establish correctness beyond their coverage. Navigation compares source
locations only, ready-state RSS is not peak memory, and maintenance compares
declared facts and sampled navigation outputs, so neither proves general
equivalence. Token counts exclude cache discounts and are lower bounds where
counters are missing, nested clocks do not give an end-to-end latency, and
Q1 leaves the route selector unmeasured.

#### Internal validity.

Two analyses of the repair study were written after we saw its outcomes, the
complete-pair estimate and the missing-outcome sensitivity; the population,
ordering, and contrasts were frozen beforehand. Haiku is reached through a
hosted alias that can change between execution dates, and missing usage
counters rule out any token-saving claim. Because the USD 1 stop rule binds,
a non-submission is an outcome of this bounded deployment, the USD 2
follow-up covers only non-Django tasks, and view construction would enter an
end-to-end cost. Only the compact and eager arms hold candidate bytes fixed. Q6 and its length-matched control reuse one cohort
and its indexes after a first execution exposed two interface defects of
ours, so they correct the interface but are not independent replications;
an earlier ten-task study estimated a 17.5-point localization deficit with an
interval spanning zero.
The navigation audit reassigned 311 of 487 observed mismatches to our
decoder, and the residual case study is AI-assisted rather than
human-annotated; rebuilding the Q6 graphs with the
corrected decoder reproduces their facts exactly. Timing shares the host
with other work and is descriptive.
